_what_this_is: Additive correction sidecar written by label paper_text on 2026-09-21. beamidp_table.json itself was NOT modified: it is generated by scripts/beamidp_table.py, and hand-editing another label's product would desynchronise it from its generator. Read this file alongside it.

corrections.recipe_in_file: planned makespan + (fleet sequential turn time - fleet Beam-IDP turn time) / n_uav = 2348.04 + 581.15/3 = 2541.76 s (reproduced by paper_text)
corrections.why_superseded: makespan is a maximum over aircraft, not a quantity the fleet shares. In this scenario the makespan is set by B2 alone, so spreading the fleet-wide turn-time saving over three aircraft understates B2's own delta and overstates the fleet figure.
corrections.replacement_recipe: for each aircraft: its own planned t_land plus the sum over ITS OWN cells of (sequential turn time - Beam-IDP turn time); then take the fleet maximum. A1 2217.64 + 218.48 = 2436.12; B2 2348.04 + 184.54 = 2532.58; B3 1992.69 + 178.13 = 2170.82.
corrections.estimate_caveat: BOTH values are extrapolations: entry and RTB legs are not re-planned and 4-D deconfliction is not re-run, exactly as this file's own _note says. The paper should lead with the directly computed turn-time saving (fleet 1696.88 -> 1115.73 s, -34.25 %) and mark any makespan figure as an estimate.

corrections.field: paper-scenario entries, 'all four strip orders identical'
entries: PAPER (same geometry at the 119.5 m cap)
corrections.status: WORDING CORRECTION - the file's own data is right, the narrative around it is not
corrections.fact: the four orders' COSTS are term-by-term equal (42.32 s / 757.4 m per HERO cell at 120 m; 42.35 s / 758.0 m at 119.5 m; fleet 126.96 s / 2272.2 m and 127.05 s / 2274.0 m), but the ORDERS differ in the n = 2 HERO cells: Beam-IDP commits [1, 0] in Z2_1_B_k1 and Z4_1_B_k1; Held-Karp commits [1, 0] in Z3_1_B_k1 and Z4_1_B_k1. By symmetry the two permutations of an n = 2 cell cost the same.

corrections.field: Held-Karp turn times quoted at 1 dp in table_md
corrections.fact: at 2 dp the Held-Karp optimum is 302.55 / 228.49 / 152.47 / 247.81 / 128.83 s for Z1_1 / Z2_1 / Z2_1_B_k6 / Z3_1 / Z3_1_B_k7. Z2_1_B_k6 is therefore 0.05 s BETTER than Beam-IDP (152.47 vs 152.52), not equal to it; only Z3_1_B_k7 is exactly equal.
corrections.consequence: Beam-IDP is above Held-Karp by 5.24 % on fleet turn time and by at most 9.11 % in a single cell (Z1_1), capturing 91.27 % of the achievable saving.

corrections.fact: the listed 'one 3000x3000 (9.00 km2) Pioneer n=6 -> makespan 3842.6 s' is a 120.0 m figure. prep_runner planned the same geometry at both caps: 120.0 -> 3842.61 s, 119.5 -> 3013.88 s (beamidp_sortie_c120.json / _c1195.json, each carrying its cap in its _note). That row is also absent from sweep_geometry.json, which stored only the three candidates that passed.
corrections.consequence: no effect on the chosen scenario (3000x3000 was rejected), but 'lowering the ceiling is nearly free' is a statement about the PAPER's cell only: on that geometry it moves makespan by -21.6 % and min separation from 190.6 to 136.5 m.
